post.description:
Vessel particulars and certificates, a vessel's US port state control history, or the controls and deficiencies of one case.

<!-- aisa-pricing:start -->

cases_to.description: Latest case StartDtTm, YYYY-MM-DD (default tomorrow, UTC). Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

id.description: psix:<VesselId>, a bare VesselId, or psix-case:<ActivityId>.

include_cases.description: Vessel ids: add case headers (default false).

vessel_id.description:
Required with a psix-case id: PSIX lists case headers per vessel.

Provider reference: minimum 1.

provider.summary: Official provider example; checked against AIsa request constraints

200.description:
One record by id. psix:<VesselId> (or the bare VesselId): getVesselSummary, getVesselParticulars, getVesselDimensions, getVesselTonnage and getVesselDocuments in parallel; with include_cases (or cases_from/cases_to, YYYY-MM-DD, default 1900-01-01 to tomorrow) also the getVesselCases headers in that window. psix-case:<ActivityId> with vessel_id: the case header (from the vessel's case list) plus its operational controls, deficiencies and inspection types. Control types pass through as published. publication_id is a SHA-256 of the record's upstream rows.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `publication_id` | string |  |
| `record` | object |  |
| `retrieved_at` | string |  |

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 5000.

200.description:
Every vessel of one segment (getVesselSummary with Flag and Service, plus BuildYear when given), sorted by VesselId and paged by offset (page_size default 1000, max 5000). Each page re-fetches the segment and compares the SHA-256 of its sorted VesselId list with the one pinned in the cursor; a mismatch fails with invalid_input issue code publication_changed. A segment over the 32 MiB response cap fails with segment_too_large: split it by build_year. Records are summary rows; records_get returns particulars, dimensions, tonnage, documents and cases.

The response contains the tool result directly.

200.description:
Vessels by name (case-insensitive substring), call sign, identification (IMO number or US official number, sent as VIN) or HIN, optionally narrowed by flag, service and build_year; at least one of name, call_sign, identification or hin is required. Exact name matches first, then by name; returns the first limit (default 50, max 500) and the total.

200.description:
Cheap version check. PSIX publishes no version, date or hash, so this hashes one getVesselSummary segment: by default the fixed canary segment UNITED STATES / Freight Ship / 2007; any flag, service and build_year segment on request. Returns the SHA-256 of the sorted VesselId list (the value a records_list cursor pins, as publication_id), a SHA-256 of the canonical summary rows (content_hash) and the record count. An empty canary segment is upstream_unavailable.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `canary_segment` | boolean |  |
| `content_hash` | string |  |
| `content_hash_algorithm` | string |  |
| `endpoint_url` | string |  |
| `file_urls` | string[] | Always empty: PSIX is a query service with no downloadable file. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `publication_id` | string | Equals segment_sha256: PSIX has no publication signal. |
| `publication_signal` | string |  |
| `published_at` | object |  |
| `publisher_hash` | object |  |
| `record_count` | number |  |
| `retrieved_at` | string |  |
| `segment` | object |  |
| `segment_hash_algorithm` | string |  |
| `segment_sha256` | string |  |
| `size_bytes` | number |  |
| `source_url` | string |  |
| `wsdl_url` | string |  |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

value.content_hash_algorithm: sha256 of the sorted canonical summary rows (fields sorted, name=value, tab separated)
value.segment_hash_algorithm: sha256 of the sorted VesselId list, one id per line (what a records_list cursor pins)
